name: FX_Hearth_Fire

textures.channels: RGB straight colour (sRGB) + alpha; 8 x 8 frames of 256 px, row by row from the top left

source_note: the frames are generated by the build script (seeded, deterministic); the .blend holds the dusk review scene with the mid frame on a card
dresses: hearth fire: a 0.8 m flame with swaying, breaking tongues, looping exactly over 64 frames; sits on the fireplace logs
status: source delivered; not imported into Unreal, no effect asset built
known_weaknesses: PARTIAL. Synthesised from scrolling noise through a tapering column, not a combustion simulation: tongues rise and break plausibly but there are no detached flamelets curling over, no embers or sparks, and no logs (the fireplace prop has those). A flipbook, not an effect: 64 frames of 256 px on one 2048 px atlas for a camera-facing billboard. It is drawn in 2D, so it casts no light, has no depth against the scene (soft-particle fade is engine work), and seen from above it is still a side view. The beauty render is the mid frame on an emissive card at dusk, not a volume. No Niagara system, material or light is authored here.
